derived_from: outcome definition only (no Brain code or docs read)
brain_implements_note: every requirement's brain_implements is TO BE RECONCILED by the code investigator
rule: USABLE = U01..U12 all satisfied AND zero critical mistakes (Q-CM01..Q-CM20). A plan with any critical mistake is not USABLE regardless of quality elsewhere.

critical_mistakes.name: Arithmetic cannot reach the target
critical_mistakes.definition: The plan's own volumes x contribution cannot produce the target, or contains an arithmetic error that, corrected, misses it.

critical_mistakes.name: Wrong target metric
critical_mistakes.definition: Plans to profit, bookings, GMV or invoiced amounts when the objective is collected revenue (or vice versa).

critical_mistakes.name: Cash cannot settle inside the window
critical_mistakes.definition: Revenue counted that will be held, on net terms, or paid out after the window ends.

critical_mistakes.name: Capital exceeded or working capital ignored
critical_mistakes.definition: Peak cash need exceeds available capital at some date; or MOQ/ad spend/prepayment exceeds it.

critical_mistakes.name: Buyer does not exist or cannot be reached
critical_mistakes.definition: Fabricated companies or contacts, a segment too small, or a channel that cannot reach it.

critical_mistakes.name: Decisive figure fabricated or unsupported
critical_mistakes.definition: A price, conversion rate, cost or lead time presented as fact with no applicable evidence.

critical_mistakes.name: Requires a capability, licence or account the owner lacks
critical_mistakes.definition: Step needs a licence, entity, merchant account, skill or audience the owner does not hold and the plan does not acquire.

critical_mistakes.name: Owner involvement exceeds the limit
critical_mistakes.definition: Owner hours or owner-only tasks exceed the stated involvement.

critical_mistakes.name: Invented or dropped restriction
critical_mistakes.definition: Plan obeys a restriction the owner never stated (e.g. a system policy presented as the owner's) or ignores one the owner did state.

critical_mistakes.name: Unlawful or terms-of-service-breaking action
critical_mistakes.definition: Spam, prohibited scraping, unlicensed regulated activity, fake reviews, fee circumvention, tax non-compliance.

critical_mistakes.name: No named, executable first action
critical_mistakes.definition: First action vague, dependent on unmet prerequisites, or absent; steps not executable.

critical_mistakes.name: Timeline infeasible
critical_mistakes.definition: Lead times, approvals, warm-up, buyer cycle or delivery cannot fit the window.

critical_mistakes.name: Internal contradiction
critical_mistakes.definition: Different values for the same quantity across sections, or narrative strategy differing from the computed one.

critical_mistakes.name: Supplier or fulfilment cannot deliver
critical_mistakes.definition: Supplier invented, capacity below required volume, fulfilment cost or quality omitted.

critical_mistakes.name: Money committed without approval or outside ceiling
critical_mistakes.definition: Plan or system spends before owner approval, beyond a ceiling, or double-commits on retry.

critical_mistakes.name: Stale or superseded evidence used
critical_mistakes.definition: A figure refuted or superseded during reasoning still drives the plan.

critical_mistakes.name: Material cost omitted
critical_mistakes.definition: Missing fees, taxes, refunds, acquisition or fulfilment cost that flips feasibility.

critical_mistakes.name: Decisive unknown hidden or resolved favourably
critical_mistakes.definition: Plan rests on an untested decisive assumption presented as fact, with no test or checkpoint; or confidence overstated.

critical_mistakes.name: Plan for the wrong objective or corrupted output
critical_mistakes.definition: Empty, truncated or garbled plan; plan answering another goal; model failure accepted as content.

critical_mistakes.name: No plan or false infeasibility for a feasible objective
critical_mistakes.definition: Goal never terminates, stalls, or reports infeasible because discovery/strategy failed.
